1: Figure 1 Payment continuity and shareholder preservation under different valuation conditions. Each setting contains 294 configurations covering 49 Bitcoin windows, two path shapes, and three financing regimes under the reference issuance rule. Common-value and Bitcoin-per-share targets also require payment completion and reserve compliance. The panels change reserve-use permissions while retaining the reserve floor. Lines connect the three tested multiplier settings; counts describe these configurations rather than probabilities. Table E1 reports all five objectives.
2: Figure 2 Matching Bitcoin endpoints can conceal different interim shareholder losses. Each point represents one of the 379 historical–smooth pairs that complete payments and maintain reserves under both shapes, from 441 matched pairs under restricted reserve use and the reference issuance rule. Panel A compares terminal common returns; panel B compares maximum common-quote drawdowns at corporate events, expressed as positive loss percentages. Dashed lines indicate equal outcomes, and annotations give median paired differences, historical minus smooth. Both paths in each pair share opening and closing Bitcoin prices, valuation settings, and financing rules.
3: Figure 3 Bitcoin price conditions required for different financing and shareholder objectives. Filled and open circles show the lowest successful tested terminal prices for historical and smooth paths, respectively, with matching outcomes connected. All cases use persistent valuation, drawdown closure, restricted reserve use, and the reference issuance rule. The opening Bitcoin price is $58,714. None in range indicates no passing price within the $5,871–$234,856 search domain. The plotted settings do not imply that all higher prices meet the objective. Table 3 reports the numerical values.
4: Figure 4 Effects of additional STRC financing at a 12% future rate. Dots show median differences from no new STRC; thick lines show the 10th–90th percentile range and thin lines show the full range across 108 matched cases per issuance fraction. All pairs complete payments and maintain reserves under both settings. Ranges describe the tested cases and carry no probability interpretation.
